A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same clarification-training framework. Their full text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison. Numerical inconsistencies are identifiable reporting issues rather than missing material.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA experiments across three model families, including preference-training comparisons, data-source ablations and selective-clarification results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical study and adds scoring-method and clarification-decision comparisons in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The original exact-match preference procedure is retained under the name Match. Section 4.1 adds a likelihood-based variant that ranks clarifying questions by summed gold-answer likelihoods after simulated clarification, providing a limited extension to the scoring procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ-Open and AmbigQA for factoid QA and clarification decisions. The added comparisons use the existing coverage; no new dataset, domain or interaction scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated Likelihood and Clarify-or-Direct-Ans SFT comparators; the latter was previously described only as an intermediate model. Section 5.1 and Appendix B add ProCoT and PPDPP to the previously random-only decision comparison. Starling and Ours are retained as RM and Match.

E3.justification: V2 adds ambiguity-classification accuracy against human labels and protocols for the new comparators: instruction-tuned models for ProCoT and an SFT-only auxiliary classifier for PPDPP. The original 1,960-question evaluation split, primary F1/turn metrics and established training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds controls examining likelihood versus exact-match scoring and SFT versus DPO for selective clarification. Appendix B reports ProCoT's always-clarify failure on Gemma and Llama3. The existing human/model-data and joint/separate-model ablations and example cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions describe significance using 10,000 samples and p < 0.01, with bold entries marking differences. V2 introduces no additional seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result entries for Likelihood, selective SFT, ProCoT/PPDPP and ambiguity accuracy. Existing values also change beyond percentage conversion: Gemma sampled-direct ambiguous F1 changes from 0.172 to 17.9%. Llama3 selective F1 changes from 0.365 in v1 Table 4 to 25.1 in v2 Table 6, conflicting with 29.1 in v2 Table 1. V2 also prints Match ambiguous F1 as 3.17 in Table 1 versus 31.7 in Table 2. These discrepancies limit performance interpretation.

T1.justification: V2 displays the DPO objective for the training method already used in v1. This is additional explanation; the interaction definitions and exact-match aggregation remain unchanged, with no new theoretical argument, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The evaluation framework, double-turn preference contribution and QA improvement claims remain. V2's abstract adds a quantified claim of 3% better accuracy in deciding when to clarify over existing methods; v1 already claimed selective clarification but lacked this comparative headline.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly interprets better answer decisions despite weaker ambiguity recognition as selecting useful clarification. Section 7 adds requirements for transferring the framework to other tasks, while removing v1's substantive discussion of human-annotator expertise, interpretation coverage, evaluation cost and reliability.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents ProCoT's instruction-tuned models and PPDPP's SFT-only training on gold dialogue-act labels, including how predictions control the existing response generator. Original hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, dataset counts, code/data access statement and licensing are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the PPDPP reference, Deng et al. (2023b), and explicitly contrasts its QA/preference-optimization approach with Andukuri et al.'s simulated-persona and filtered-SFT approach. The ProCoT paper was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and selected method, results and related-work paragraphs, adopts RM/Match terminology, and inserts an Additional Experiments appendix. The main narrative order remains intact. Affiliations, acknowledgments and the conference header also change.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 are substantially redesigned with model families arranged across columns and scores presented on a percentage scale; Table 1 adds grouped rows and shading. Selective-decision results are redistributed between revised Table 4 and new Appendix Table 6. Figure 3 is relabeled and relocated, while existing appendix displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added likelihood/SFT controls and ProCoT/PPDPP comparisons strengthen v1's limited evidence for clarification decisions and help distinguish QA utility from ambiguity recognition. The gain is tempered by numerical transcription errors, unresolved Llama3 F1 disagreements between Tables 1 and 6, and removal of the substantive human-evaluation caveats from Section 7.
